intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades in Borthwickrig, and it's easy to see why. Whether you're adapting a home for easier access, modernising a tired bathroom, or simply investing in something that adds real value to your property, a professionally installed wet room delivers on all fronts. Borthwickrig's housing mix — from sturdy old stone cottages to newer builds on modern estates — means every installation comes with its own set of considerations, and getting the groundwork right is everything. Done properly, a wet room should last decades without a leak or a damp patch in sight.
localContext: Borthwickrig sits in Midlothian and its housing stock tells a story of different eras built side by side. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up much of the village present some genuine challenges when it comes to wet room installation. Stone walls and older floor structures often need more preparation work before a fully waterproofed wet room system can be laid, and subfloor levels may need adjusting to achieve the correct fall toward the drain. Modern estates in and around Borthwickrig tend to have more straightforward timber or concrete floor construction, which can simplify the tanking process, though each property still needs a proper assessment. It's also worth knowing that Borthwickrig sits in a moderately hard water area. This means limescale will gradually build up on fixtures, screens, and drains over time, so choosing quality fittings with good limescale resistance and committing to a regular cleaning routine will protect your investment and keep everything looking sharp for longer.
serviceDetail:
A wet room installation in Borthwickrig follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding each stage helps you know what you're paying for and why cutting corners isn't an option. The process begins with a full survey of your existing bathroom space. The installer will check the subfloor condition, the wall construction, drainage options, and the position of existing plumbing — all of which directly shape the design and the cost. In older Borthwickrig stone properties, this stage sometimes throws up surprises like uneven floors or walls that need building out before a proper waterproof membrane can be applied.

Once the design is agreed, the room is stripped back completely. The subfloor is then prepared and a former or screed is laid to create the correct gradient — typically around 1:80 — so water flows cleanly to the drain rather than pooling on the floor. Next comes the tanking stage, where a waterproof membrane system is applied to the floor and all walls to a minimum height, usually at least 1.8 metres. This is the most critical part of the job and should never be rushed.

With tanking complete, wall and floor tiles are laid, the drain is fitted and sealed, and plumbing connections are made for the shower, any bath if retained, basin, and toilet. A final check ensures drainage is working correctly before the room is finished and handed over. From first fix to completion, most Borthwickrig installations take between five and ten working days depending on complexity.
pricing: Wet room installation in Borthwickrig typically falls in the range of £6,000 to £12,000 for a full conversion, and where you land within that range depends on several factors. Older stone-built properties and period cottages often sit toward the higher end due to the additional preparation work needed on floors and walls. The size of the room, your choice of tiles and fixtures, and whether you're retaining any existing sanitaryware all affect the final figure. A straightforward installation in a modern estate property with a concrete subfloor and mid-range finishes might come in closer to £6,500–£8,000, while a premium finish with high-end tiling and bespoke fixtures in an older property could reach £10,000–£12,000 or more.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickrig and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for a job like this. Local installers will have worked in similar stone-built properties and period cottages before, so they won't be caught off guard by the quirks that older construction brings. They'll know the right approach for the local building conditions, they're easier to contact if a follow-up is needed, and their reputation in the community depends on doing good work. For a premium installation that you'll live with every day, that local knowledge and accountability is worth a great deal.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickrig?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more careful preparation than a modern property. Stone walls and older floor structures need thorough assessment before tanking begins. An experienced installer will check subfloor strength, manage any levelling work needed, and ensure the waterproofing system is fully suited to the construction. It's done regularly in Borthwickrig's older housing stock with excellent results.

faqs.q: Will limescale be a problem in my Borthwickrig wet room?
faqs.a: Borthwickrig is in a moderately hard water area, so limescale will gradually build up on glass screens, chrome fittings, and drain covers if left unchecked. Using a squeegee after each shower, applying a limescale-resistant coating to screens, and descaling fittings every few months will keep things looking clean and extend the life of your installation considerably.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwickrig?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. Simpler jobs in modern properties with straightforward floors can be quicker, while older stone-built properties in Borthwickrig that need additional floor preparation or wall building work may take longer. Your installer should give you a realistic programme once they've carried out a proper survey.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a property in Borthwickrig?
faqs.a: A well-executed wet room generally adds value and appeal, particularly in a smaller settlement like Borthwickrig where quality finishes stand out. Buyers increasingly see wet rooms as a premium feature, especially when they're well designed and properly waterproofed. The return is strongest when the installation uses quality materials and complements the character of the property, whether that's a period cottage or a modern home.

localParagraph: Wet room installation in Borthwickrig, Midlothian, presents a range of considerations that reflect the character of this Scottish settlement and its surroundings. Borthwickrig sits within a region where water hardness tends to be mixed, so installers should factor in appropriate tanking systems and specify fittings with sufficient resistance to both mineral deposits and the corrosive effects that softer water can sometimes accelerate on metalwork. Scotland's climate also means that moisture management and proper waterproofing are particularly important, especially in older properties where existing damp issues could be compounded by inadequate wet room preparation.
